steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Over here, Doctor.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Squeeze in a bit, so this dessert cart's in front.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Finally, a chance to catch my breath.

options: Thanks for going through all that.
Whose dessert cart is this?

steps.name: Gap-Toothed Girl
steps.text: You must be here for the ceremony, seniora!

steps.name: Gap-Toothed Girl
steps.text: W-Would you like to try my ice cream?
Before Mon3tr can even refuse, the little girl gleefully shoves a cup of ice cream into her hands.

steps.name: Gap-Toothed Girl
steps.text: I-It's not a flavor you can get anywhere else in Laterano—

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (I can take her out. Nobody would notice.)
As Mon3tr gives you this paranoid suggestion, she plops a spoonful of ice cream into her mouth without thinking about it.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Wow. That's really good...

options: *ahem* Could you tell me your name, kid?

steps.name: Gap-Toothed Girl
steps.text: It's got my answer for me, confessor.

steps.name: Idida
steps.text: Dadadeedeeda, I'm called Idida.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: You named yourself after the dessert cart's music?

steps.name: Idida
steps.text: Don't be silly! I customized it to sound like my name!

options: Did you know those Guards, Idida—
Aren't you scared of this lady, Idida—

steps.name: Idida
steps.text: Wow! I've never heard a confessional speak like that before!

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: It's the latest model.

options: (Sighs)
Looks like she buys that explanation.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Were you helping cover for us just now, Idida?

steps.name: Idida
steps.text: Yep... Because all of Laterano needs to change!

steps.name: Idida
steps.text: That's what you think too, right?!

steps.name: Idida
steps.text: W-Was I just imagining things? You're the first person to say my sugar-free carbonated-water-flavored ice cream was tasty, seniora!

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Well, that explains why it's so refreshing.)

steps.name: Idida
steps.text: Mamma and Tata were right, this is a rocky road I walk... But I've finally found a little bit of success!

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Mind... explaining a bit more?

steps.name: Idida
steps.text: 'Desserts connect every Lateran'—but if you eat too much sugar, not only are you gonna get bad teeth, even your halo will start getting cavities!

steps.name: Idida
steps.text: Tata's a dentist. Every time he says that, people think he's just trying to get more business for his clinic.

steps.name: Idida
steps.text: But right now, my halo, err, kinda feels like the rotten tooth I just lost. It's making me feel... not so good...

steps.name: Idida
steps.text: I believe it's the Lord giving me a revelation!

steps.name: Idida
steps.text: So I'm gonna practice what I preach! I'll change Laterano's eating habits, and rebuild our connections with the power of sugar-free ice cream!

options: That's a grand dream you got there, Idida.
Would you support this young citizen's vision, madam?

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Mind if we take a walk together? I'd like to hear more about this... connection between halos and tooth decay.

steps.name: Idida
steps.text: O-Okay!

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (We should be able to avoid the guys chasing us with this kid around. You need to get in touch with Exusiai ASAP, Doctor.)

options: I'm trying.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Hey there, Leader!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Sounds like you were able to loosen that comms control thingy, since we're having a long-distance call and all.

options: It's not entirely a good thing, Exusiai.
This means everything in the dream is collapsing faster.
This means the calamity in reality is getting worse.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Ugh. Yeah, I figured as much.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: These guys have nearly all the non-Sankta holed up in the Shrine of Nurtury. They want to put on an even bigger Nativity.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: First time around, an arborbeast got a halo. This time, they want to give everyone halos...

spans.text: First time around, an arborbeast got a halo. This time, they want to give

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: I dunno how they're gonna do it, but this kind of change is a bit too quick and crazy.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: The way you explained it, Leader, whatever happens in this dream will eventually become reality?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Ugh. Yeah, I figured as much.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: The way you explained it, Leader, this big, ugly building really is poking up out of Laterano's streets, and it's spewing out haloed monsters to chase people around?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Sounds like reality's a lot scarier than the dream...

options: What you said is what I saw, Exusiai.
But some people are starting to awaken.
Variables in reality are making the dream skip some steps.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Man, this is WAY too complicated for me. Just tell me: what's the worst thing that might happen?

options: Laterano might stop existing entirely.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Whew, yeah, that's a REALLY big deal!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Well, no matter the situation, I can still find the jerk behind all this and free everyone from 'fake Laterano', right?

options: We're limited to keeping you clear-headed and free to move around.
The restrictions Mon3tr and I are under haven't been lifted yet.
Mon3tr and I are still looking into other leads.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Got it! Leave Laterano's troubles to a Lateran like me!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Oops, gotta keep my voice down. The grand Nativity's about to start, and it wasn't easy finding a chance to sneak in, heheh.

spans.text: Oops, gotta keep my voice down. The
Nativity's about to start, and it wasn't easy finding a chance to sneak in, heheh.

options: Mon3tr and I will keep tearing up the streets.
Mon3tr and I will keep eyes off of you.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Say, how did the two of us meet again?

spans.text: the two of us meet again?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: One of Sora's releases? Texas's birthday party? That time Penguin Logistics crashed into the Lungmen office while cracking down on the Bloodhammer gang?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Oh, or was it that time I was planning on stealing a few sick old racing beasts when I ran into you on your way to buy their freedom?

options: We definitely met in Lungmen, at least.
I don't think it was any of those.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Must've been... what, five years ago now?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Well, here's to yet another beautiful partnership, Leader.

options: Likewise, Exusiai.
Stay safe, Exusiai.

steps.name: Gun-Knight
steps.text: Everyone is in position, Reverend Patrizion.

steps.name: Gun-Knight
steps.text: Next, we will coordinate with the shrine patrol to clear the surrounding streets, lock down the intersections, and ensure nobody is wandering about.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Gratias.

steps.name: Gun-Knight
steps.text: Every gun-knight gathered together, our ammunition allocations and fire restrictions fully lifted... There's never been so big an event in the history of our order, has there?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: The Nativity is of great significance to Laterano.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: The black snow on the ice of Sami, the hole in the sky above Leithanien, even the raging tides that dash against the coast, are all in alignment with the true calamity that has been prophesied.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Imagine how terrifying such a disaster would be.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: When that time comes, two-hundred-odd gun-knights taking to the field would be like a child throwing stones into the sea.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: I fear our holy city, which has stood tall for millennia, will fade away.

steps.name: Gun-Knight
steps.text: The Pontifica Cohors and the Notarial Hall are still pursuing Lemuel and her co-conspirators.

steps.name: Gun-Knight
steps.text: There is something else you must know... The nurturer who was guiding Mostima and Fiammetta was just attacked.

steps.name: Gun-Knight
steps.text: Would you like to go and check the scene, Reverend?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: My post... is here.

steps.name: Nurturer
steps.text: The time has come.

steps.name: Nurturer
steps.text: All our Liberi brethren, please go to the Hall of Enlightenment.

steps.name: Nurturer
steps.text: The time has come.

steps.name: Nurturer
steps.text: Over here, please. Once the other races have been bestowed their halos, the Matriarch shall mend the broken halos and wings of the fallen angels, so that we may all regain empathy with our people.

steps.name: Nurturer
steps.text: It has begun, Matriarch.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: I thank you all. You have forsaken nearly all rest since the establishment of this shrine.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: There have been many mishaps since the last Nativity. We must advance our plans. This shrine's mission must be seen to completion as quickly as possible.

steps.name: Nurturer
steps.text: To this day, we have walked the same path, Matriarch. This is something we realized long ago.

steps.name: Nurturer
steps.text: Oh, yes, there was one other thing on my mind. Today's ceremony is all about bestowing halos on the non-Sankta rather than a birth, so why are we still using the name 'Nativity'?

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Is there a better term for it?
The nurturers lead the peoples of various races into the Hall of Enlightenment, converging toward its center. The grand procession is like a herd of migratory beasts, yet none speak a word.
There is only the rhythmic tinkling of countless comfort bells.
As if in response, the Matriarch lifts her head toward the crowd.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Henceforth, all who are sheltered by the holy city shall share one destiny, entwined into a singular whole. Can this be called anything but the rebirth of Laterano?
The crack of shattering glass cuts through the calming chimes of the comfort bells.
A bullet from a sniper rifle. Its source is unknown, but it flies straight for the Matriarch's sightless eyes—
Blinding sunlight seeps in.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: That strange couple at the door...

steps.name: Notarial Hall Employee
steps.text: Looks like they're deciding where to go to dinner using a roulette wheel. Interesting idea, isn't it?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Mhm. So they're the ones...

steps.name: Notarial Hall Employee
steps.text: ...who wish to adopt you.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: But why won't they come in and tell me that themselves...?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Oh, I get it. They don't want to put too much pressure on me.

steps.name: Notarial Hall Employee
steps.text: Now why do you think that?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Because they're pretending to fiddle with their guns while actually looking our way.

steps.name: Notarial Hall Employee
steps.text: Haha, nothing ever gets past you, does it? Yes, I reached out to them before they came here.

steps.name: Notarial Hall Employee
steps.text: Your parents were in that caravan raid... and the Notarial Hall's been trying to arrange things with a few families for the better part of a year now, but nobody's bitten yet.

steps.name: Notarial Hall Employee
steps.text: You're the strongest child I've ever met, En, but you've still got a long way to go, and we can't let a kid live all by herself.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I know, seniora.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I'm not annoyed or anything, it's just... If I'm going to accept the kindness of others, I'm going to have to be a good kid myself! It's really, really important!

steps.name: Notarial Hall Employee
steps.text: Well, the long and short of it is, they wanted me to tell you that they really like you.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I also think they're really... Can I have a week, no, three days? I'll think things over.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Once I make a decision, I won't go back on it!

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Is this the one that feels right for you?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Mhm.

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: Whoa, a sniper rifle. If it was me, I would never choose that one...

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: No, when it's my turn in a few years, I'll pick lots and lots and lots of guns!

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Haha, sounds good.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Well, I have to remind you that this fellow's been sitting here a few years now. Never been picked. Best think it over.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Hmm... It's really quiet.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: No, no, what I meant was, this sort of gun's different from the others. Truth be told, it's not very suited to you lively Sanktas.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: When you're on the battlefield, you won't get many chances to fire it. You'll have to make every shot count.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Whether you're trying to protect something or destroy it, you'll need to have a sharper eye, a sharper mind, and take on more risks and costs...

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Because you can pull the trigger, or let it go, but you can't afford to hesitate.
Today is Lemuen's birthday. Today, she chooses her patron firearm, giving even more meaning to this already extremely important day to the Sankta.
The gunsmith speaks with all seriousness. Her mother and father behind her and all her friends are silent. Even the ever-vivacious Lemuel keeps her mouth closed like a good girl for once.
Despite the silence, Lemuen knows they are all looking right at her.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: This is the one, Master Pag. Please guide me through selecting the other parts.

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: Nice!

steps.name: Lemuel
steps.text: You don't need to worry about it not having the chance to fire, Master Pag. You could smack people real hard with a gun this big, and my sis is super strong!

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Through the spiritual light, even the darkest stain can be cleansed. With a pious heart, even a savage monster can wade out of the mud.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: —Hah—

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Put that down, Captain. I've got you in my sights.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: You're unstable, I can sense it. Calm down. That thing's affecting your mind. It's evoking your disappointment in Laterano.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I know you submitted your resignation before we left... But even if you're determined to return to the wilderness, right now, you're still one of us.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Think about the fried cheese we ate before we left, okay? Think about that fowlbeast hat Fiammetta got you, the soft and downy one.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: My disappointment in Laterano... No, no... Far from it! He showed me how Laterano can save everyone.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: None of us know if what you're seeing is the truth of reality, or illusions and lies. Mostima will be here soon. She has a way to get that thing off you.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: We can start looking into its secrets afterwards. Alright?

spans.text: We can start looking into its secrets

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: There is no 'afterwards'! It's fading away! I must hold onto it... You know it's no illusion, Lemuen! It's certainly not lies!

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: You saw those people locked in stasis, outside of time, down in the underground palace. Those who do not die yet do not live.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: You heard what that mad Sarkaz said to his shadow: 'The future shall have no secrets.'

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: So you should understand. What we've found is the key to time itself. What I saw was a revelation. A future where even the most savage of monsters can be saved...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Your Arts are running haywire, Andoain. That thing's eating away at you—

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: If that future exists, I must find the path that leads to it.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I won't let go! I need to know more!
Andoain keeps his grasp on the oddly-shaped staff. Light condenses into solid form, and engulfs the entire cave.
I have a lot of chances to pull the trigger, Lemuen thinks.
But amidst the chaotic, roiling waves of emotion, Lemuen finally finds the thread of rationality running through Andoain's mind.
They have broken bread with one another. They have built bonds with one another. They understood one another, entrusted their lives to one another. Their empathic link was stronger than any other.
In that final moment, Lemuen confirms her friend has not been swept away in that unfathomable chaos.
She loosens her finger on the trigger.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Dammit! Look out, Lemuen!

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Haah—

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Keph, Matriarch of the Shrine of Nurtury... Hit.
The rooftop wind whips wildly at the sniper's cheek. She does not blink. Her hand doesn't move in the slightest.
She hears. She sees. She thinks. She judges.
She doesn't have many chances to fire. She has to make every shot count.
She can pull the trigger, or let it go, but she can't afford to hesitate.
Before that crucial moment, she and her gun do not speak.
Lemuen the Silent.
She looks through her scope once more, double-checking what she sees in her sights. It is proof she pulled the trigger.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Compared to the ones in the vast lands, the statues oft seen in Laterano are the more incomprehensible, Cardinal.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Paradise has shaped our faith, so peculiar that it has become somewhat distorted.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: The souls of the living praying for survival, as they traverse Catastrophe and suffering... such is the most basic face of faith.
No, there's never a dull statue in Laterano.
By life is faith shaped. Gun-wielding saints towering over the streets do not represent disdain for calamity and suffering. We have simply chosen to take up a different mindset when confronting them.
Through her scope, from far in the distance, Lemuen can finally see that all the statues in the shrine, their heads bowed and their hands clasped, are facing only the pious Matriarch as they pray.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Keph... If she really is a horrible monster, then it's unlikely a bullet will do any real damage.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: But at the very least, it'll let the people in the shrine see what's so unnatural about her, and create an opportunity for you... El.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: The rest, I leave to you!

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Senior Amos?

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Seniora Lemuen... my location has been compromised.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I'll come back you up right away.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: N-No need.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: The shrine patrol is already here, a-and the gun-knights, too... There's a lot of them!

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: I'll hold down the street corner. Get yourself out of the building before they surround the place.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: What about you?

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: It's too late for me.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: They've started firing. Looks like our deduction was right. This cannot be a place just for birthing babies...

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Anyway, did you take care of the target?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Yes. Got her in one.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: That's good, that's good, haha. At least this way, I managed to save a few people, stop a few things that needed to be stopped. Can't be useless forever now, can I?

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Well then, vale. Go do what you need to do, Seniora Lemuen.

spans.text: Go do what you need to do, Seniora Lemuen.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Actually, I've got a question I wanted to ask you... Funny, it's only once you can't hear it that I finally dare to ask it.
A glitch in the comms terminal must be keeping the line open. And so, the man goes on at length, chattering into the microphone.
Lemuen hesitates for a moment, then chooses to be silent.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Was I really that useless?

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: I never thought about it before. Even though it took nearly all I had just to become a small-time investigator for the Seventh Tribunal, and I never got a promotion during my decade or so there...

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: It seems us Laterans never doubt ourselves on that front. It's like we naturally have a hundred million ways to keep ourselves happy and satisfied.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: I know someone who made sticks for lollipops. He'd take several types of paper tape and twist them together into rainbow-colored sticks... Made nearly no money out of it. He did it simply because he knew children loved them.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: But ever since I found out Aurela had been banished from Laterano, and there was nothing I could do about it, I haven't been able to feel even a microsecond of satisfaction with myself.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: 'You're completely useless, Amos.' That's all I could think... Like how you can never forget the taste of the very first terrible dessert you ever ate, haha.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: I thought that maybe, with a few more years, I could use my seniority to muddle my way to the Legati and go on a trip to Bolívar.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: I couldn't save her in the name of Laterano. Not even I can forgive her for what she did. I just want to see her again, and apologize for that argument we had.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: After so many long years of waiting, I finally got my chance, but... it was all just a dream...

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: A dream's fine, too.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: If it's all a dream, then I don't have to worry about anything. Maybe getting shot here doesn't mean anything in reality!

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: When I was younger, I got fifth place at the Seventh Tribunal new joiner shooting competition, you know!

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: I even met Aurela that day at the range...

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: It's a shame we weren't able to save each other.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I'd say that, at the very least, you're a great investigator, Amos.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Oh, you were still on the line, Lemuen...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: It's time to wake up.

steps.name: Nurturer
steps.text: Is the funeral complete, Andoain?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: It is.

steps.name: Nurturer
steps.text: The Hall of Enlightenment is this way. You seem to be going the wrong way.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Am I?

steps.name: Nurturer
steps.text: The Nativity has begun, and the Matriarch is waiting for you. Where are you planning to go right now?

steps.name: Nurturer
steps.text: Your emotions are... rather unstable.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: No. I've never felt more clear-headed. I'm not going the wrong way, either.

steps.name: Nurturer
steps.text: I ask that you accompany me to see the Matriarch, Andoain.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Looks like we arrived right on time.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Mostima, Fiammetta, you...

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: What, am I supposed to be like the other Liberi, pushed back into the herd by the guards, no matter how I protest?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Or should I be really looking forward to seeing if my halo gets to be a square or a circle?

spans.text: looking forward to seeing if my halo gets to be a square or a circle?

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Speaking of, I'm curious how they're going to mend the fallen angels' halos...

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Mostima!

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Sorry, got sidetracked. You owe us an explanation, Andoain.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Gathering up all the non-Sankta, forcing changes on their bodies... I thought this sort of stuff only happened in those shady Columbian tech companies full of mad scientists.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Is this what you meant when you said it was 'about the future, about a possibility for Laterano'?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Is this what the Matriarch promised you?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I have strayed from my path. That, I cannot deny.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Laterano wove a beautiful dream for us all. I was trapped too deep, and took too long to awaken.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Still talking nonsense even now?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: The other guards will be here soon.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Dammit. Do you think we can get close to the Matriarch if we use him as a hostage, Mostima?

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Maybe? She does trust him a lot. I'd be a little worried if we left it all up to El.

spans.text: trust him a lot. I'd be a little worried if we left it all up to El.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I can sense... a multitude of emotions, growing by the second. The number of people with empathy in this shrine is increasing...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: The Nativity has begun. It's no use, even if you subdue the Matriarch right now.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: We must go do what we still can.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I'll think of what to do about this ceremony that should not exist.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: But it's likely to lead to great chaos... It should buy you the time to evacuate our people.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: What's your plan?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Why do you think we'll trust you, Andoain? Seriously, a babbling lunatic who already betrayed his friend once, saving everyone?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: You don't need to trust me.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Pity will not save the people. I don't have that kind of power.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: All someone who has walked the wrong path of obsession can do is to save himself.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Wait, Andoain. Take this.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: A bomb?

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: El gave it to us to draw the guards' attention.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: But if you really are going to stop this ceremony that shouldn't exist, like you said...

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: You'll need it more than us.
Andoain walks past the pair, heading straight for the depths of the shrine.
His steps are slow, but Fiammetta makes no move to stop him.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: You okay with letting him go?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: He's reliable when he sticks to a handful of words instead of a full-on parable.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: True, true.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: The situation's too damned weird. Not like we have any better options at the moment.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: There's a whole lot of people coming this way. Probably chasing Andoain.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Help buy him some breathing room. I'll get even with him after this is all over.

spans.text: Help buy him some breathing room. I'll get even with him

steps.text: The shrine's very first nursery.
Once, with a heart full of hope, it was here he tended to an unfortunate mother, day after day.
Now, the child she left behind has clambered up onto a comfort bell, the sparkling droplets of water on his freshly-washed wings refracting the lamplight. Just like a dream.
The arborbeast does not mind his caretaker's prior outburst. He calls out happily as always, inviting Andoain to play with him.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Insignificant trifles and grandiose feats are but a hair's breadth from one another. You have labored for many years over this grueling journey of yours. You should not let such a meaningless difference stay your steps.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: I will need you to lift your spirits, for aside from caring for this mother and child, there are more deeds that must be done.
An insignificant nurturer. A heaven-piercing shrine.
The former could grit his teeth, harden his heart and refuse the young beast's invitation, but this minor act of rebellion would do nothing to shake the foundations of the latter.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I should be doing more... I must do more!

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: But how do I shake the pillars of this shrine? How do I erase a miracle that has already occurred?

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: The Shrine of Nurtury... This towering edifice was not built in a day. It began as a simple, ordinary nursery.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Our nursery...

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Did we start with the blueprints of such an imposing shrine? No. We merely wished for a safe, comfortable room for that mother...

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: And yet, its frenzied evolution led to what it is now.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: That is how a future where all are saved can sprout from our faith.

spans.text: is how a future where all are saved can sprout from our faith.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: This was the very first nursery in the Shrine of Nurtury. This was the starting point of this grandiose building.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: This is where you and I placed our faith.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: And so, Keph, I'll tear my faith apart.
Andoain examines the bomb Mostima gave him closely. It has been imaginatively cobbled together from all sorts of daily necessities, its face decorated with a bright splash of graffiti.
He cannot remember what the girl who made this looked like. They might have met once or twice. They might never have met at all. He can only remember Lemuen recounting her deeds countless times over.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I was never alone as I sought a way through this trail of thorns, was I?
Without the slightest hesitation, he lights the fuse.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: (Cheerful chirp)

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I understand that you are no longer sad and suffering, my child. But do you not sense danger, even as this room is about to explode?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Or... are you simply uninterested in this as well?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Does Laterano no longer need us to feel fear?

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: (Puzzled chirp)
The arborbeast flies down to the ground, rubbing against Andoain's trousers in confusion.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: If we cannot feel fondness, fear or torment for all that life has to offer, how can we speak of revering it?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I should have asked you this, my child.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: But it was I who brought you here. You could even say you were born in answer to my vision.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: This is our penance. A lesson for the both of us.
Andoain bends over, and cradles the arborbeast into his arms.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: That gunshot—

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I am so very glad to hear the sound of your gun this time around, Lemuen.

Sparks bloom wildly across the nursery. A giant comfort bell clatters as it falls, its sonorous notes adding to the clamor. The explosion engulfs the room, devouring the graceful balance of light and shadow.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Was this realm a dream, or an obsession?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Once, you had a flock of brothers and sisters following behind you. They were rejected, harmed, insulted, desecrated. They named you Guide, and walked the long path with you.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Yet here in this Laterano, which you believed equal and selfless, you forgot them. And so I ask...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: How should this community you long for be shaped?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: How should this holy city you yearn for be rebuilt?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: What path is it you walk, Andoain? To what answers does it lead?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: If this is a dream, then I shall wake. If this is obsession, then I shall shatter it.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Let us only speak of redemption after that.
The flames swallow the entire nursery. The arborbeast flaps his wings furiously. There is no fear in his eyes, as though he is simply dancing.
Yet Andoain still covers his eyes out of habit.
In this final moment, Andoain hears a bell, clear as day.

steps.name: Nurturer
steps.text: Are you alright, Matriarch?

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Hngh...

steps.name: Nurturer
steps.text: The ceremony has been interrupted. The entire Shrine is shaking, and that explosion just now...

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Is an evacuation underway?

steps.name: Nurturer
steps.text: Y-Yes... There is a Liberi wearing a Pontifica Cohors uniform and a fallen angel leading our people to safety.

steps.name: Nurturer
steps.text: Only half of the non-Sankta have successfully acquired halos. I will ask the patrol to have them reconvene right away—

Like the cracking of bamboo, the explosion reverberates out from the depths of the shrine. The peal of a bell from parts unknown drowns out the chimes of the comfort bells. Chaos reigns as countless people flock to the exit.
The towering edifice sways as the blast wave finally reaches the Hall of Enlightenment.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Let them leave.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Forcing them to stay will only harm them irreparably.

steps.name: Nurturer
steps.text: The shrine is collapsing, Matriarch...

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: No. What is collapsing is not only the shrine, but also the answer we sought with it.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Gather the other nurturers. Everyone must leave at once.

steps.name: Nurturer
steps.text: I will have the guards escort you out.
The Matriarch steps down from the dais.
The wind. Amidst the chaos, she hears the sound of the wind clearly from above her head, where there should only be praying statues and spotless stained glass.
Hey hey hey, over here!
You're not getting away that easily!
The Matriarch lifts her head. She cannot see who is approaching her, but her voice has an infectious quality to it. Almost instinctively, she stretches out her arm.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: I've been hanging onto this window for two hours already! If you don't get off that stage, my arms are gonna fall off!
Exusiai holds on tight to the Matriarch. The world spins, and the two of them tumble to the floor.
What they fall onto is not solid ground, but rather some odd softness. It is like falling into fog, yet also like falling into water.
Exusiai senses a great force pushing her outwards, one that is definitely not just the explosion. Could this frail-looking woman really be that strong?

She forces herself to open her eyes. She isn't sure when it happened, but the arm she is holding onto has become the jagged limbs of a beast. The Matriarch's gentle face has disappeared under the water.
They look at one another across the boundary between truth and lies. On her side of the line, the bell atop the Tower of Revelations rings, clear as can be.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: I did figure you weren't as pretty as you looked early on, but my imagination never prepared me for this. Not even Ancient Forge had anything as crazy-looking as you!

spans.text: I did figure you weren't as pretty as you looked early on, but my imagination never prepared me for
had anything as crazy-looking as you!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Well, at least I don't have to worry about ripping your arm off!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: My friends had to bust their butts to give me this chance...

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: So get out of there already! You have no right to hide away in a dream! You have no right to hide... in our Laterano!!
